summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and a history of alcohol abuse was admitted for a Puestow procedure due to obstructing pancreatic duct stones causing ductal dilation and severe pain. He underwent successful surgery with Roux-en-Y drainage and intraoperative ultrasound guidance. Post-operatively, he experienced inadequate pain control initially, which was managed by adding methadone and later transitioning to oral hydromorphone and gabapentin. He developed transient confusion and a single nonepileptic seizure-like episode on post-operative day 7, attributed to narcotics and managed with dose tapering. His diet advanced from NPO to regular, and he ambulated early. A CT scan revealed a right hilar lymph node requiring bronchoscopy and findings suggestive of aspiration. He was discharged home with home health services, on a regimen including pain medication, Viokase, and a nicotine patch, with follow-up planned with surgery and primary care.
problems: Other opiates and related narcotics causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
